paragraphs: My name is Joshua Chappell and I am applying for the Marketing Manager position. Your posting says this is not a posting job, and that is why I am writing. I have spent seven years on active construction sites with a camera, and the rest of my time running the marketing behind the footage.

The content side is the part most applicants can show. I have filmed construction, trades, and industrial work across the Valley and cut it into brand films that actually sell the craft; you can see that work at the Construction Work link above. I shoot it, edit it, grade it in DaVinci Resolve, build the motion graphics in After Effects, and mix the audio. I hold an FAA Part 107 drone license, so the aerial reveal of a finished backyard does not require booking a vendor.

The marketing side is where I separate from most shooters. At Charter One I created and led a social initiative that earned more than 20x the engagement of standard content, and a campaign that raised ad click-through by over 200%. At Lightbox I ran Meta ads with pixel tracking on site, and closed $10k in new business from one optimization channel. I hold a Master's in Marketing with an analytics specialization, so qualified leads, ROAS, and signed revenue are the numbers I already work in.

The third part of the job is the one people skip. I built my company on referral relationships with custom home builders, developers, and realtors; I filmed model homes for Blandford Homes and photographed listings for agents. I know how to walk into a builder's office and leave with a project. I also organize community events with my local church, so representing a brand in a room is familiar ground.

Four things on your preferred list are construction and real estate marketing, Meta Ads with lead-generation results, FAA Part 107, and motion graphics, color grading, or sound design. I have all four. I live in Mesa, twenty minutes from your Gilbert office, and I have shot in Arizona summer heat at 5 a.m. and at dusk more times than I can count.
Thank you for your time. I would welcome the chance to walk you through the work.

He meets all four nice-to-haves: construction and real estate marketing, Meta Ads lead generation with pixel tracking, FAA Part 107, and motion graphics, color grading and sound design.

gaps: TikTok, a named channel, isn't in his record. His answer: 'The short-form craft (hooks, pacing, retention) carries over from Reels and Shorts. TikTok distributes content differently, and I'd learn it fast by running it.'

Award submissions and magazine features are listed duties, and Envy won two Pinnacles in 2026. His answer: 'I haven't run award submissions before. I'd own them, and the project films and photos I shoot are what they're built from.'
His writing is real but not proven as copywriting. His answer: 'I script and storyboard my shoots, and I'm glad to show my copy in the paid assessment.'

He hasn't run LinkedIn as a company channel. His answer: 'I haven't managed a company LinkedIn page. Builders and architects are the audience there, so I'd set it up early with the same content and tracking habits.'
He has only partly directed outside vendors. His answer: 'I've directed crews of five to twenty on shoots. Hiring freelancers against a budget is newer for me, and I'd keep it tight.'

reference.jd_text:
## Full job description

Most marketing jobs ask you to make ordinary work look interesting. We have the opposite problem. Envy Pools builds lazy rivers, grottos, massive rock waterfalls and multimillion-dollar backyards across the Phoenix metro, and our marketing has not caught up to what we build. We are hiring the person who closes that gap.

**About Envy Pools**

Envy Pools is a luxury pool and outdoor living design-build company founded in 2018. We work with homeowners, custom homebuilders and developers on resort-style pools, custom water features, architectural structures and complete outdoor environments. We are a two-time 2026 Pinnacle Award winner, and we are growing.

See the work: www.envypools.com and @envypoolsaz on Instagram.

**The role**

You will own Envy's marketing: the strategy, the content, the channels and the results. This is not a posting job. One day you are on an active build with a camera. The next you are cutting a reveal, planning a campaign, reviewing ad performance, sitting down with a builder who should be sending us projects, or deciding with ownership what to push next.

**What you'll do**

- Set the marketing and social media strategy and run it across Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, YouTube and LinkedIn
- Work with in-house media who photo and video on active job sites and finished projects, from excavation to final reveal
- Produce Reels, TikToks, YouTube Shorts and long-form project films built on strong hooks and real storytelling
- Write captions and copy that drive reach, engagement and qualified inquiries
- Get out and build relationships in person with custom home builders, architects, designers and realtors, and turn them into a [unreadable]
- Represent Envy at industry events, builder [unreadable]

[not captured in screenshots]

- Direct outside videographers, photographers and designers when a project calls for it
- Run paid advertising, or manage the specialists who do, and answer for the return
- Track audience growth, traffic, leads and conversion, then report what is working and change what is not
- Produce award submissions, magazine features and co-marketing with our partners
- Use AI and automation tools to work faster without lowering the standard

**What you bring**

- A portfolio of video and social campaigns you personally shot, edited or ran, with results you can show
- Hands-on photography, videography and editing skills (Premiere Pro, Lightroom, Photoshop, CapCut, Canva or comparable)
- A working understanding of how Instagram and TikTok distribute content: hooks, retention, shares
- Strong writing
- Working knowledge of paid social, marketing funnels, lead tracking and analytics
- A track record of bringing in business face to face: partnerships, referral relationships, events
- Self-drive: you set the plan, run several projects at once and don't wait to be told
- Comfort working on active construction sites outdoors in Arizona, including early-morning and dusk shoots
- A valid driver's license and reliable transportation to job sites across the Valley

A degree is not required. Proof of work is.

**Nice to have**

- Experience marketing luxury, construction, architecture, real estate, hospitality or automotive brands
- Meta Ads experience with lead-generation results you can point to
- FAA Part 107 drone certification
- Motion graphics, color grading or sound design

**How success is measured**

By outcomes, not post count: qualified reach and audience growth, watch time and shares, website traffic, qualified inquiries, marketing-attributed leads, referral partners brought on, return on ad spend, and signed revenue from projects marketing brought in.

**Why this one is different**

- **The material.** Dramatic construction, complex engineering and finished environments that most creators never get access to.
- **Direct line to ownership.** You work with the people who make the decisions. Good ideas move fast.
- **Room to build.** The goal is to make Envy one of the most recognized luxury pool builders in the country. You would be building that, not maintaining an account.

**Compensation and benefits**

- $65,000–$90,000 a year, based on experience
- Health insurance, paid time off and paid holidays
- Full-time, in person: based at our Gilbert office, with shoots on job sites across the Phoenix metro

**How to apply**

Apply through Indeed with your resume and answer the screening questions, including a link to your portfolio or the accounts you have run. Applications without work samples will not be reviewed.

Finalists complete a short paid skills assessment.

Envy Pools is an equal opportunity employer.

Pay: $35,000.00 - $85,000.00 per year

Benefits:

- Health insurance
- Paid time off

Application Question(s):

- Paste a link to your portfolio or the accounts you've personally run. Only include work you shot, edited or managed yourself.
- Link the best video you personally shot and edited. What were the numbers, and why did it work?
- What did you learn in the last 90 days that made your shooting, editing or marketing better? How did you learn it?
- Tell us about a time your marketing brought in revenue you could measure. What was the dollar amount or number of closed deals, and how did you track it?
- Describe the last time you brought in business face to face: events, networking, partnerships or referral relationships. Who did you go after, what did you do, and what came of it?
- Our best projects come through builders, architects, designers and realtors. If you started Monday, who would you go meet in your first 30 days, and how would you get in the door?
- Tell us about something you built or launched that nobody asked you to. What was it, and what happened?
- Look at our Instagram, @envypoolsaz. What's the first thing you'd change, and why?
- This role means regular shoots on active construction sites across the Phoenix metro (summer heat, early mornings, dusk) plus in-person meetings and events, some evenings. Can you do this? Yes or no.

License/Certification:

- Driver's License (Required)

Ability to Commute:

- Gilbert, AZ 85297 (Required)

Work Location: In person

red_flags: The posting gives two pay ranges: $65,000-$90,000 in the text and $35,000-$85,000 in Indeed's pay field. Find out which one is real before you spend a day on the paid skills assessment.
Few benefits are listed: health insurance, paid time off and paid holidays. No 401(k) or other retirement plan is mentioned, so ask.

One person does three jobs: making the content, running paid marketing, and bringing in builder and realtor referrals face to face. The posting mentions no marketing team, so you would likely be the whole department.
Expect regular shoots on active construction sites in Arizona summer heat, early mornings and dusk, plus in-person meetings and some evening events (screening question 9).
No one checked what employees say, so turnover, how the owners manage, and who did marketing before are all unknown. Ask about them in the first call.
research.bottom_line: Going only by the posting, this looks like a small, growing company with the owners closely involved. It seems to be hiring its first real marketing lead. That means a lot of room to build and direct access to the decision-makers, but no team, few listed benefits, and two pay ranges that don't match. What it's actually like to work there hasn't been checked. Look at Glassdoor and Indeed reviews yourself, and get the real pay number before the paid assessment.
